title: Behind Ibrahim's station
hookLine: two units of prayer behind the station of Ibrahim (2:125)

lines: HE STEPS OUT OF THE CIRCLE.
cards: The seventh circuit ends at the corner of the stone. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ has gone around the House, and the crowd is still turning.
Jabir ibn Abdullah, who told the story of that pilgrimage in a report kept in Sahih Muslim, says what came next.
The Prophet stepped out of the circle and walked a short way to a spot near the Ka'ba, reciting a line from the Qur'an as he went. Then he stood, with that spot between him and the House, and prayed.

teach.h: TAKE AS YOUR PLACE OF WORSHIP.
teach.b: First, the verse he recited. It's in surah two, and Pickthall's translation reads: "Take as your place of worship the place where Abraham stood (to pray)." The Arabic name is maqam Ibrahim, the station of Ibrahim.
Tradition says it's a stone Ibrahim stood on while he and his son built the House; today it sits in a small enclosure near the Ka'ba. Second, what the Prophet did there.
Jabir says he placed the station between himself and the House and prayed two rak'ahs, two units of prayer.
Jabir also reports what he recited in them: two short surahs, the one that begins Say: He is Allah, One, and the one that begins Say: O disbelievers.
Abdullah ibn Umar, in Sahih al-Bukhari, gives the same order: the circuits, then two rak'ahs behind the station, then on to the next rite. Third, the posture of the place.
After the moving, the crowd, the circling, the reaching for the stone, the pilgrim stops where Ibrahim is said to have stood, and prays toward the same House.

teach.h: THE CIRCLE TURNS INTO A LINE.
teach.b: The circle turns into a line, one person facing one direction.

teach.h: A WEEK OF STEPS, THEN A PAUSE.
teach.b: Fourth, look back, because this is where the week lands. The boundary. The two white cloths.
The restraint they stand for. Here I am, said out loud for miles. Seven circuits around the center.

A kiss, a touch, or a raised hand at the corner. And now two quiet rak'ahs at the place of the man who, in the Qur'an, built the House and called the people to it. Each piece this week has been one step.
This one is the pause between them.

how: After completing tawaf, pilgrims pray two rak'ahs behind the station of Ibrahim if there is room, or elsewhere in the mosque when it is crowded, often reciting al-Kafirun and al-Ikhlas.

practice: If you're Muslim and pray, pray two rak'ahs now, and if you know them, recite the two short surahs the Prophet chose.
If you don't pray, stand still for a minute facing one direction, any direction, on purpose, feet steady and hands at rest, and let the week's movement settle into one place.
